content:
Let A be “All men are cannibals” and B be “All women are vegetarians.”

- If both A and B are true, then all men are cannibals and all women are vegetarians. Then every speaker would be making a true statement, but cannibal men would have no false statement to make. Impossible.
- If both A and B are false, then every speaker must be a cannibal, so there are no vegetarians, contradicting that A false requires a vegetarian man. Impossible.

The valid cases:
- A true, B false: all men are cannibals, and at least one woman is a cannibal. Vegetarian women say A. Maximize by taking 1 cannibal man, 1 cannibal woman, and 48 vegetarian women.
- A false, B true: at least one vegetarian man, and all women are vegetarians. Take 2 men, one vegetarian and one cannibal, and 48 vegetarian women.

Both valid cases give at most 48 vegetarian women.

\boxed{48}
